findings.title: should_block? has race condition / non-atomic increment
findings.body: self.should_block? reads a record, increments match_count in Ruby, then saves. Under concurrent signups with the same blocked email, this read-modify-write is not atomic and can lose updates (lost increments). Should use update_counters or an atomic SQL UPDATE ... SET match_count = match_count + 1.

findings.title: BlockedEmail.should_block? called on every validation and mutates state as a side effect
findings.body: should_block? is invoked from validate_each, which can run multiple times per request (e.g. once for user.valid? check in UsersController#create and again on user.save). This causes match_count to be incremented and last_match_at updated multiple times for a single signup attempt, inflating statistics and causing extra DB writes during validation, which is also a surprising side effect for a validator to perform directly against the DB on every validation pass.

findings.title: Exposing full errors hash and attribute values to client without filtering
findings.body: The create action now exposes user.errors.to_hash and user.attributes.slice(name, username, email) in the JSON response. While email/username/name are already visible to the user, returning the full errors hash changes the API contract for any consumer and could leak more validation detail than before (e.g. internal error keys) without the previous explicit review of what's exposed.

findings.title: rejectedEmails never cleared, causing valid emails to be permanently rejected within the modal session
findings.body: Once an email is pushed into rejectedEmails (e.g., due to being blocked), it stays rejected forever within that modal session even if the underlying blocked status changes or the user corrects something else. There's no mechanism to clear previously rejected but now-fixed emails, and because rejectedEmails is a prototype-level array (Em.A([]) at the class level), it may also be inadvertently shared across controller instances if not properly reset per instantiation, leading to stale rejection state across signups in the same page session.
